q: 1. The centre of gravity of a trapezium with parallel sides a and b lies at a distance of y from the base b. The value of y is
explain: The vertical distance of the centroid of a trapezium from base 'b' is calculated as (h/3) * ((2a + b) / (a + b)).

q: 3. M.O.I. of a solid cone about an axis passing through its C.G. and parallel to base is
explain: The formula for the mass moment of inertia of a solid cone about a transverse axis through its CG is (3/20)M(r² + h²/4).

q: 4. Polar moment of inertia of an equilateral triangle of sides x is given by
explain: For an equilateral triangle with side x, Ip = x⁴ / 16√3.

q: 5. The materials which have the same elastic properties in all directions, are called
explain: Isotropic materials have identical mechanical properties (like E and G) regardless of the direction in which the property is measured.

q: 6. The under mentioned type is simple strain
explain: Tensile, compressive, and shear strains are all primary/simple types of deformation corresponding to their respective stress types.

q: 7. The unit of strain is
explain: Since strain is the ratio of two lengths (change in length / original length), the units cancel out, making it a dimensionless quantity.

q: 8. Young's modulus may be defined as the ratio of
explain: Young's Modulus (E) defines the stiffness of a material under axial loading (linear stress/linear strain).

q: 9. When a bar of length l and diameter d is rigidly fixed at upper end and hanging freely, then total elongation produced in the bar due to its own weight is
explain: The elongation of a prismatic bar due to its own weight is given by $\delta l = \gamma l^2 / 2E$, where $\gamma$ (or w) is weight per unit volume.

q: 10. When a circular bar tapering uniformly from diameter d1 at one end to d2 at the other end, is subjected to an increase in temperature (t), then the thermal stress induced is
explain: For a tapering bar, the stress varies along the length. The maximum thermal stress developed when the ends are fixed is (α * t * E * d1) / d2.

q: 11. When a body is subjected to three mutually perpendicular stresses, of equal intensity, the ratio of direct stress to the corresponding volumetric strain is
explain: Bulk Modulus (K) is the ratio of direct stress to volumetric strain when a body is subjected to equal stresses in all three directions.

q: 12. Within elastic limit, shear stress is ___________ shear strain.
explain: According to Hooke's Law for shear, shear stress is directly proportional to shear strain within the elastic limit.

q: 13. Shear modulus is the ratio of
explain: Shear Modulus (or Modulus of Rigidity, G) is defined as the ratio of shear stress to shear strain.

q: 14. The ratio of elongations of a conical bar due to its own weight and that of a prismatic bar of the same length, is
explain: Elongation of prismatic bar = γL²/2E. Elongation of conical bar = γL²/6E. The ratio is (1/6) / (1/2) = 1/3.

q: 15. When a rectangular beam is loaded transversely, the maximum compressive stress is developed on the
explain: As explained in Q. 296, the curvature causes the top layer of a simply supported beam to shorten, resulting in maximum compressive stress.

q: 16. For the materials which do not have a pronounced yield point... the yield point is taken to be
options: stress corresponding to 0.2% strain from the stress strain curve
the stress at which the permanent set reaches the value 0.2%
average of ultimate strength and actual breaking stress
explain: For materials like aluminum or high-strength steel, the proof stress (yield point) is determined using the 0.2% offset method.

q: 17. The energy stored in a body when strained within elastic limit is known as
explain: Strain energy is the internal work done by the force to deform a body, stored as potential energy while within the elastic limit.

q: 18. The stress induced in a body, when suddenly loaded, is ............ the stress induced when the same load is applied gradually.
explain: For a suddenly applied load, the instantaneous stress reached is twice the value of the static stress produced by the same load.

q: 19. The strain energy stored in a spring, when subjected to maximum load, without suffering permanent distortion, is known as
explain: Proof resilience is the maximum strain energy a body can store without undergoing permanent (plastic) deformation.

q: 20. If the strains in the three principal directions are εx, εy and εz, the volumetric strain will be
explain: Volumetric strain (e_v) is the sum of the linear strains in three mutually perpendicular directions.

q: 21. The maximum shear stress will be equal to
options: one half of the algebraic difference of the maximum and minimum principal stresses at the point
the intensity of shear stress acting on the major principal plane
the shear stress acting on the planes in the direction of two principal directions
explain: τ_max = (σ1 - σ2) / 2, where σ1 and σ2 are the major and minor principal stresses.

q: 22. The ratio of strengths of a rivet in double shear to that in a single shear will be
explain: In double shear, there are two planes resisting the shear force, effectively doubling the strength compared to a single shear plane.

q: 23. The torsional formula is valid if the shearing stresses ............
options: are within the shearing proportional limit
are caused due to twisting moment applied only at the free end
explain: The torsion formula assumes linear elastic behavior, meaning the shear stress must be within the proportional limit of the material.

q: 24. Within the elastic range of a tensile test the deviation from Hooke's law and some after effects may be noticed. This is due to ............
options: material does not at all obey Hooke's law
elastic limit is greater than ultimate strength
explain: Thermo-elastic effects involve small temperature changes during loading/unloading that can cause slight non-linearity even within the elastic range.

q: 25. When a cylindrical specimen of a ductile material is subjected to compression ............
options: it ultimately assumes the shape of a flat disc
it fails by fracture like a brittle material
it fails immediately after starting of loading
explain: Ductile materials under compression undergo significant plastic deformation (bulging) without fracturing, eventually flattening into a disc shape.

q: 26. What is the core of a section ............
options: portion where a compressive force applied causes no tension anywhere
the central portion of the cross-section of similar shape but half the area
area where compressive force will not cause any compressive stress
explain: The 'core' or 'kern' is the area within which an eccentric load can be applied without inducing any tensile stress in the section.

q: 27. For keeping the stress wholly compressive, the load may be applied on a circular column anywhere within a concentric circle of diameter
explain: The kern of a solid circular section of diameter d is a concentric circle of diameter d/4.

q: 28. If a beam is loaded transversely, the maximum compressive stress develops on
explain: For typical sagging (downward transverse load), the top fiber is in maximum compression.

q: 29. Find the elongation of a bar if c/s area of bar is A, length l, applied load p, modulus of elasticity of material is E
explain: Standard elongation formula: δ = PL/AE.

q: 30. Thrust is induced in case of
explain: Thrust (axial force along the member) develops from the component of an inclined load along the member's axis.

q: 31. If the elasticity of the material is zero then the material is said to be
explain: Zero elasticity means the material shows no elastic recovery — it deforms plastically.

q: 32. An orthotropic material has
options: different properties in three perpendicular directions
explain: Orthotropic materials have distinct material properties along three mutually perpendicular axes (e.g. wood).

q: 33. The moment of inertia of triangular section b×h about the c.g. is
explain: Standard formula: I_cg = bh³/36 for a triangular section.

q: 34. The shear center may be defined as
options: the point through which the resultant of the shear stress passes
the point about which the moment of shear flow of section is zero
the shear force in that direction
explain: The shear center is the point of application of transverse load through which no twisting occurs — the resultant shear stress passes through it.

q: 35. The shear center in the case of a T-beam section is
options: at the C.G. of the section
at the neutral axis of the section
on the C.G. horizontal plane and away from C.G. within the leg projections
explain: For a T-section, the shear center coincides with the centroid due to its axis of symmetry.

q: 36. The phenomenon of decreased resistance of material due to reversal of stress is called
explain: Repeated/reversed stress cycles progressively weaken a material — this is fatigue.

q: 37. The property of a material by which a body returns to its original shape after removal of the force, is called
explain: Elasticity is the ability to recover original shape/size after unloading.

q: 38. The S.I. unit of modulus of elasticity is
explain: Modulus of elasticity has units of stress (force/area); the SI unit is N/m² (Pascal).

q: 39. The stress at which extension of a material takes place more quickly as compared to the increase in load, is called
explain: This describes the yield point, where strain grows disproportionately fast relative to load.

q: 40. The law which states that within elastic limits strain produced is proportional to stress producing it is known as:
explain: This is the direct statement of Hooke's Law.
